codeReview.summary: Clean, well-scoped implementation that adds .flywheel/library/ shared knowledge directory for inter-worker context sharing. Four files changed: LIBRARY_DIR constant and ensureLibraryDir() helper in paths.ts, directory creation in execution-loop.ts's run() method, a 'Shared Knowledge Library' section in the work prompt template, and 11 comprehensive tests. The code follows existing codebase patterns (matches handoffs directory creation style), has proper JSDoc, and all 5 expectedBehavior items are covered by tests. The implementation correctly adapts Droid's .factory/library/ pattern.

issues.description: ensureLibraryDir() is defined in paths.ts but never imported or called from execution-loop.ts. The execution loop inlines the mkdirSync call directly using LIBRARY_DIR. The function is only exercised by tests (tests/shared-knowledge-library.test.ts). This is dead code in production — it works, but creates a subtle inconsistency: the handoffs directory creation doesn't have a helper function, and the library directory creation has one that isn't used. Consider either using ensureLibraryDir() in execution-loop.ts (replacing the inline mkdirSync) or removing the helper and keeping tests against the inline pattern.

The Shared Knowledge Library section is placed after THREE_STRIKE_PROTOCOL and VERIFICATION_BANNED_PHRASES but before the completionSection. This placement is reasonable but the library instructions (read before starting, write before completing) are near the bottom of a very long prompt. Workers may miss these instructions given their position. Consider whether placing it earlier (e.g., after the Task section) would improve compliance. This is a prompt-design concern, not a bug.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The ensureLibraryDir() helper function in paths.ts establishes a pattern of directory creation helpers, but it's not actually used in production code. The execution-loop.ts inlines the mkdirSync call instead (matching the existing handoffsDir pattern). This creates a mixed convention — some directory creation is inline (handoffs, library in execution-loop), some has helpers (library in paths.ts). The AGENTS.md architecture notes don't mention a preferred convention for directory initialization.

summary: PASS. The shared-knowledge-library feature is correctly implemented with all 5 expectedBehavior items satisfied: (1) .flywheel/library/ directory is created during pipeline initialization in ExecutionLoop.run(), (2) work prompt includes 'read from .flywheel/library/' instruction, (3) work prompt includes 'write discoveries to .flywheel/library/' instruction, (4) prompt references environment.md and architecture.md filenames, (5) directory creation uses recursive:true so it's idempotent.
